text: A conceptual model is an explanation. <break time="0.8s" /> Usually highly simplified. <break time="0.8s" /> Of how something works. <break time="0.8s" /> It does not have to be complete or even accurate. <break time="0.8s" /> As long as it is useful. <break time="0.8s" /> The files, folders, and icons you see displayed on a computer screen. <break time="0.8s" /> Help people create the conceptual model. <break time="0.8s" /> Of documents and folders inside the computer. <break time="0.8s" /> Or of apps or applications on the screen. <break time="0.8s" /> In fact. <break time="0.8s" /> There are no folders inside the computer. <break time="0.8s" /> , those are effective conceptualizations designed to make them easier to use. <break time="0.8s" /> Sometimes these depictions can add to the confusion. <break time="0.8s" /> However. <break time="0.8s" /> When reading e mail or visiting a website. <break time="0.8s" /> The material appears to be on the device. <break time="0.8s" /> For that is where it is displayed and used. <break time="0.8s" /> But in fact. <break time="0.8s" /> In many cases. <break time="0.8s" /> The actual material is in the cloud. <break time="0.8s" /> Located on some distant machine. <break time="0.8s" /> The conceptual model is of one, coherent image. <break time="0.8s" /> Whereas it may actually consist of parts. <break time="0.8s" /> Each located on different machines. <break time="0.8s" /> That could be almost anywhere in the world.
